newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: COMMISSION REGISTERS LITIMPEKS BANK ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: COMMISSION REGISTERS LITIMPEKS BANK ISSUE.

text.p: Lithuania's securities commission said on Monday that it registered a 60 million litas share issue for Litimpeks Bank on Friday.
The commission also said in a statement that the share capital of the bank will be 64.09 million litas after the increase.
"We plan to start the distribution of the share issue on Thursday," Litimpeks Bank's deputy chiarman, Edmundas Kachkus, told Reuters.
"We also plan to name the financial advisor who will organise the distribution of the share issue on Friday," Kackus added, but declined to name the advisor at this stage.
The newspaper Verslo Zinios said last week that Norway's Balticum Managment S.A was acting as the bank's financial advisor.
"We have no doubts about the successful distribution of the whole share issue before July 1," Kackus said.
He also said that potential buyers included a Japanese invstment company with partners, a few Norwegian funds active in Lithuania and local investors.
"Each of the groups intends to acquire around one third of the issue but we think that no single investor will acquire more than a 10 percent stake," Kachkus said.
The bank has also been in talks in the past with Estonian and Polish banks.
Litimpeks Bank was shut in late 1995 at the start of a banking crisis but was reopened in June of 1996 and has been struggling to stay on its feet since.
